RECONSTRUCTION from about a dozen windows, not a transcription of the page. Square brackets mark
where the joins are uncertain or a word is supplied.

THE ENTRY AS RECONSTRUCTED:

  LOCKE, ROY  municipal politician
  [b. Toronto, Ont., c. 1920; d. Montreal West, Que., 19 September 1991, age 71]

  Roy Douglas Locke was a former mayor of the suburban Montreal community of Montreal West.
  Locke graduated from the University of Toronto and worked initially with the Young Men's
  Chris[-]tian Association (YMCA) in Toronto[ ... ] business from 1954 to 1969, then returned
  to the YMCA as director of fi[-]nancial development until 1986. He served on the town
  commission of Montreal West from 1973 to 1989, first as commissioner of recreation, then for
  12 years as mayor. Locke was particu[-]larly proud of his work in developing parks and
  protecting green spaces in the community. Locke headed the financial campaign for the Fraser
  Hickson Library in Notre Dame de Grace, Quebec, and was a di[-]rector of Camp Kanawana, a
  children's camp in the Laurentians. He is survived by his wife, Patricia, nee Binns, daughter
  Vicky Chantler and three grandchildren. (MG 20 and 21 Sep [1991])

THE ONE GAP
  Between "in Toronto" and "business from 1954 to 1969" there is unread text -- one clause at
  least, and it is the clause that would cover his Montreal years, his Kanawana camp
  chiefship of 1947 and the Westmount Branch posting of September 1954. It was not recovered.
  What can be said is that the obituary places him in business from 1954, which sits against the
  Montreal YMCA's own 1954 Annual Report recording him succeeding N. A. Millington at Westmount
  Branch on 1 September 1954. Neither is preferred; see f_4935.

  "MG" is the Montreal Gazette. The underlying obituary, Gazette of 20 and 21 September 1991,
  has not been read.
